28          A. The Parties

 1            1.      At all times herein mentioned, Plaintiffs Jewel Seperson and Hans Larsen
 2   (collectively “Plaintiffs”) are individuals who at all times referenced herein resided together as
 3   husband and wife in Santa Clara County, California.
 4            2.      Plaintiffs at all times referenced herein have owned real property commonly
 5   known as 27760 Edgerton Road, Los Altos Hills, California, and have resided in Santa Clara
 6   County at a nearby residence while their home is being remodeled.
 7            3.      Defendant Connie Lane Christy (hereinafter (“Christy”) at all times referenced
 8   herein was an individual who at all times referenced herein engaged in the business of interior
 9   design as, among other things, a designer and procurer of household furnishings and other items
10   for clients and sometimes also referred to as Connie Lane Christy ASID NCIDQ. Plaintiffs are
11   informed and believe that Christy is a citizen of the state of South Carolina, with another
12   residence in Idaho.
13            4.      Defendant Christy Collection International, Inc. (hereinafter “Christy Collection”)
14   at all times referenced herein was a corporation established and existing under the laws of the
15   State of South Carolina, with its principal place of business in South Carolina. Christy Collection
16   is one of the entities Christy used to provide interior design and procurement services to
17   Plaintiffs and others.
18            5.      At all times set forth herein, each of the defendants was acting as an agent,
19   employee or servant of each of the remaining defendants and in doing the acts alleged herein was
20   acting either as an individual or within the course and scope of such agency, employment or
21   service.
22            B. Jurisdiction and Venue
23            6.      Jurisdiction is proper in this Court under 28 U.S.C. §1332(a)(2) because the
24   amount in controversy exceeds $75,000, exclusive of interest and costs, and this lawsuit is a
25   dispute between citizens of a State (California) and citizens of the State of South Carolina and
26   Idaho.
27

28

 1           7.      Venue is proper in the Northern District under 28 U.S.C. §1391(b)(2), because a
 2   substantial part of the events or omissions giving rise to the claim occurred in the Northern
 3   District.
 4

 5

     Santa Clara County.

 8           C. Facts Common to All Claims for Relief

 9           9.      Plaintiffs met Christy in or around January, 2024, when they saw her work online

10    while Plaintiffs were in the process of planning the remodeling of their Los Altos Hills

11    residence. Christy and Christy Collection represented to Plaintiffs, among other things, that

12    Christy and Christy Collection were experts in home interior design and procurement of upscale

13    household furnishings and other items as an agent for clients from third parties throughout the

14    world and could assist Plaintiffs by providing such services to Plaintiffs at and for their Los

15    Alto Hills residence.

16           10.     On or about January 24, 2024, or shortly thereafter Plaintiffs, on the one hand,

17    and Christy and Christy Collection, on the other hand, entered a partially written and partially

18    oral agreement for Christy and Christy Collection to provide interior design services and to

19    procure household furnishings and other items as Plaintiffs’ agent from third parties for

20    Plaintiffs’ Los Altos residence in Santa Clara County, California. A true and correct copy of the

21    written agreement is attached hereto as Exhibit “1.” Based upon, among other things, Christy

22    and Christy Collection’s representations as to their expertise and services to be provided,

23    Plaintiffs placed their trust and confidence in whereby Christy and Christy Collection were

24    obligated and duty bound to act with the utmost good faith for the benefit of Plaintiffs as

25    fiduciaries.

26           11.     Pursuant to the written agreement, Plaintiffs immediately provided Christy and

27    Christy Collection an approximate $30,800 deposit payment by wire transfer and they met at the

28    premises. On or about May 23, 2024, Plaintiffs sent to Christy and Christy Collection

 1   $659,189.87 as an additional payment so that defendants could purchase household furnishings
 2   and other items from third parties on Plaintiffs’ behalf for their Los Altos residence.
 3          12.      In emails and text messages exchanged between Christy and plaintiffs between
 4   January 19, 2024 and December 9, 2024, defendants promised to order furnishings for plaintiffs’
 5   residence and to assist in the design of such residence, and to store all furniture and materials that
 6   defendants had purchased for plaintiffs until they were ready to accept delivery at their
 7   residence.
 8          13.      Due to delays and remodeling, in or around late February, March, and again on
 9   April 30, 2025, Plaintiffs requested that Christy and Christy Collection provide Plaintiffs,
10   among other things, item inventories, purchase invoices, receipts, storage locations and the like
11   for items allegedly purchased and stored by Christy and Christy Collection on Plaintiffs’ behalf
12   and asked that all such items be delivered to Plaintiffs’ possession to a location in Sunnyvale,
13   California. Christy and Christy Collection refused to deliver said items to Plaintiffs absent
14   payment of alleged storage fees to which Plaintiffs never agreed. Christy and Christy Collection
15   further refused to provide Plaintiffs among other things, item inventories, purchase invoices,
16   receipts, storage locations and the like as Plaintiffs requested, to substantiate defendants’ claims
17   to have purchased items for plaintiffs’ residence and having incurred storage fees for these
18   items on plaintiffs’ behalf.
19          14.      Christy and Christy Collection also have not returned any funds to Plaintiffs and
20   remain in possession of items, if any, that defendants allegedly purchased on Plaintiffs’ behalf.
21

 1            41.    Defendants made the promises and representations specified in paragraph 12
 2   above to plaintiffs in emails and text messages exchanged between Christy and plaintiffs
 3   between January 19, 2024 and December 9, 2024.
 4            42.    In reliance on these promises and representations, plaintiffs provided defendants
 5   with an initial $30,800 deposit and then sent defendants $659,189.87 by wire transfer on May 23,
 6   2024 to pay for furniture and other materials that defendants were supposed to purchase for
 7   plaintiffs’ residence.
 8            43.    Plaintiffs are informed and believe that Defendants’ representations to plaintiffs
 9   about procuring furniture and materials for plaintiffs’ home were false when made and that
10   defendants have not in fact purchased such items nor incurred storage fees with respect to such
11   items. Plaintiffs’ belief is based upon the fact that they have repeatedly asked defendants to
12   provide a list of the items purchased, invoices, and other evidence that they have purchased such
13   items and incurred storage fees on behalf of plaintiffs, but defendants have not provided any such
14   evidence despite such requests.
15            44.    The conduct of Defendants, including failing to inform Plaintiffs of information
16   concerning the property procured by Defendants and otherwise, constitutes a concealment, fraud
17   and deceit due to knowing the false misrepresentation as to procurement, holding, and delivery
18   of Plaintiffs’ assets with intent to deceive Plaintiffs.
19            45.    When Defendants made these representations, promises and concealments, they
20   knew or should have known them to be false and intended to deceive and defraud Plaintiffs and
21   to induce Plaintiffs to act in reliance on these representations and concealments.
22            46.    Plaintiffs at the time these representations, promises and concealments were made
23   by Defendants, and at the time Plaintiffs took the actions herein alleged, were ignorant of true
24   facts.
25            47.    As a proximate result of the fraudulent conduct of Defendants, Plaintiffs have
26   been damaged and continue to be damaged as described herein.
27            48.    Defendants’ conduct was intentional, fraudulent, and malicious, warranting the
28   imposition of exemplary damages against defendants.
